goalLabel: Build muscle, lose a little fat
summary: Eat about what you burn, keep protein high and let your hands set the portions. Nothing to weigh, nothing to count.

why.title: Eat about what you burn, protein high
why.text: Lifting 4 days a week builds the muscle and protein feeds it. Eating what you burn, not dieting, lets a little fat come off slowly while you get stronger.

source.text: your goal is to build muscle and lose a little fat

why.title: Hands, not numbers
why.text: A palm of protein, a fist of vegetables, a cupped hand of carbs, a thumb of fat. Close enough is good enough, and a loose day changes nothing.

source.text: following a diet exactly is hard, and you’ll have loose days

why.title: Heart-healthy foods
why.text: Fish twice a week, legumes 3 times, lean lamb at most twice, olive or canola oil over butter, nuts most days, little added sugar and salt.

source.aside: The numbers stay with your doctor.

reason.title: Protein a day
reason.note: Lifting goals: 1.6 to 2.2 g per kg a day (Morton 2018). At 83.5 kg that is 134 to 184 g; the tick is for days with at least 134 g.

tips.title: Cook double at dinner
tips.text: Lunch is your hardest meal. Cook 4 palms of protein tonight and box half: tomorrow’s lunch is ready before you leave.

tips.title: Keep a lunch shelf at work
tips.text: A tin of tuna, a tin of chickpeas, wholegrain wraps and a bag of nuts make a 5-minute lunch on any day.

tips.title: Give fish two fixed days
tips.text: Say Tuesday and Friday, so it happens without thinking. Oily fish such as salmon, trout or sardines are the best picks.

tips.title: Eating out, or a loose day
tips.text: Pick the plate that looks most like your hands: protein, vegetables, then carbs. Next meal, protein first and back to the template. Never skip a meal to make up.
